title: Non-Solvability of Sₐ is Upward Closed Under Injections
description: The order-theoretic dual of the parent. Where the parent proved solvability of permutation groups is downward closed in the carrier — {n | IsSolvable (Perm (Fin n))} is the down-set {0,1,2,3,4} — this entry proves the complementary face: non-solvability is upward closed. The structural engine perm_not_solvable_of_embedding is the exact contrapositive of the parent's perm_solvable_of_embedding: if α ↪ β and Perm α is NOT solvable, then Perm β is NOT solvable, because an unsolvable permutation group cannot embed into a solvable one. From it, perm_not_solvable_mono and alternating_not_solvable_mono give the cardinality face, and not_solvable_perm_card_isUpSet packages {n | ¬ IsSolvable (Perm (Fin n))} as the up-set {n | 5 ≤ n}. Together with the parent the two faces partition ℕ as an order-complementary down-set / up-set pair (solvable_unsolvable_partition), meeting at the Abel–Ruffini boundary where the least unsolvable cardinality 5 is the successor of the greatest solvable one 4 (five_is_min_unsolvable_card, boundary_is_successor).

overview.historicalContext: That S₅ is non-solvable is the algebraic obstruction underlying the Abel–Ruffini theorem, and the reason the general quintic is not solvable by radicals. But the threshold cannot rise as the degree grows: because Sₘ embeds in Sₙ for m ≤ n (fix the last n − m points), once S₅ fails to be solvable every Sₙ with n ≥ 5 contains a non-solvable subgroup and so is itself non-solvable. The parent entry exposed the down-set structure of the solvable cardinalities; this entry isolates the dual statement that the non-solvable cardinalities are an up-set, the precise sense in which non-solvability, once it appears, is permanent under enlarging the carrier.
overview.modernSignificance: Subgroup-closure of solvability has a contrapositive of equal structural weight: a group with an unsolvable subgroup is itself unsolvable. Applied to the functor Perm on finite sets and injections, this makes non-solvability a covariant (upward) property of the carrier — the mirror of the parent's contravariant solvability. Stating it via the same injective hom Equiv.Perm.viaEmbeddingHom keeps the argument cardinality-free; the up-set packaging (5 is the minimum non-solvable cardinality) is the order-theoretic seed of Abel–Ruffini, and pairing it with the parent's down-set exhibits the full solvability dichotomy of symmetric groups as a single order-complement at the boundary n = 5.
overview.problemStatement:
Working with the permutation functor $\mathrm{Perm}$ on finite types and injections, prove that non-solvability is upward closed: if $e : \alpha \hookrightarrow  eta$ and $\mathrm{Perm}\,\alpha$ is not solvable, then $\mathrm{Perm}\, eta$ is not solvable. Derive the cardinality form ($|\alpha| \le | eta|$ and $
eg\,\mathrm{IsSolvable}(\mathrm{Perm}\,\alpha)$ force $
eg\,\mathrm{IsSolvable}(\mathrm{Perm}\, eta)$), its alternating analogue, and package $\{n \mid 
eg\,\mathrm{IsSolvable}(\mathrm{Perm}(\mathrm{Fin}\,n))\}$ as the up-set $\{n \mid 5 \le n\}$. Finally exhibit this up-set and the parent's solvable down-set $\{n \mid n \le 4\}$ as order-complements partitioning $\mathbb{N}$, meeting at the Abel–Ruffini boundary $5 = 4 + 1$.
overview.proofStrategy: Three stages, each a thin specialization of the one before. (§1) The engine perm_not_solvable_of_embedding is proved by contradiction in three lines: assume Perm β is solvable, register it as a typeclass instance, and apply the parent's perm_solvable_of_embedding e to contradict the unsolvability of Perm α — the literal contrapositive of subgroup-closure, with no cardinality. (§2) perm_not_solvable_mono converts |α| ≤ |β| into an embedding via Function.Embedding.nonempty_of_card_le and feeds §1; alternating_not_solvable_mono sandwiches the symmetric result between two applications of the grandparent bridge sym_not_solvable_iff_alternating_not_solvable. (§3) not_solvable_perm_card_eq_ge_five rewrites the grandparent threshold through Fintype.card_fin into the arithmetic predicate 5 ≤ n, after which upward closure (not_solvable_perm_card_isUpSet) and minimality (five_is_min_unsolvable_card) are each a single omega; solvable_unsolvable_partition and boundary_is_successor then assemble the two faces into a complementary partition meeting at n = 5.
keyInsights: The contrapositive *is* the proof. perm_not_solvable_of_embedding is the exact contrapositive of the parent's perm_solvable_of_embedding — non-solvability flows *up* an injection precisely because solvability flows *down* one. No new mathematical content is introduced; the direction of inheritance is reversed by reading the same subgroup-closure statement backwards.

The structural engine is cardinality-free. perm_not_solvable_of_embedding never mentions the number 5 or any cardinality; it depends only on Equiv.Perm.viaEmbeddingHom_injective and solvable_of_solvable_injective. The threshold 5 enters only in §3 when the abstract carrier is specialized to Fin n via Fintype.card_fin.

For finite types an embedding is exactly a cardinality inequality. Function.Embedding.nonempty_of_card_le makes |α| ≤ |β| yield α ↪ β, so cardinality co-monotonicity (perm_not_solvable_mono) is not a separate theorem but the same structural ascent with the embedding produced on the fly.

The sign extension is transparent to non-solvability. alternating_not_solvable_mono routes A_α → S_α → S_β → A_β through two uses of sym_not_solvable_iff_alternating_not_solvable, so the alternating and symmetric families gain and lose solvability in lockstep — the index-2 inclusion A_n ◁ S_n never obstructs the inheritance.

omega discharges the order theory once non-solvability becomes 5 ≤ n. After not_solvable_perm_card_eq_ge_five reduces the group-theoretic predicate to an arithmetic one, upward closure and the minimality of 5 are each a one-line omega — the order-theoretic content is entirely linear arithmetic on ℕ.

The two faces are a single order-complement. solvable_unsolvable_partition shows {≤4} and {≥5} partition ℕ, and boundary_is_successor records 4 + 1 = 5: the greatest solvable cardinality and the least unsolvable one are adjacent, so the Abel–Ruffini threshold is encoded as a successor relation rather than an isolated fact about S₅.

conclusion.summary: Nine machine-checked theorems establish that non-solvability of Perm is upward closed under injections, the order-theoretic dual of the parent's downward closure of solvability. The engine perm_not_solvable_of_embedding is the exact contrapositive of perm_solvable_of_embedding; from it the cardinality co-monotonicity (symmetric and alternating), the up-set packaging {n | ¬ IsSolvable (Perm (Fin n))} = {n | 5 ≤ n}, the minimality of 5, and the complementary partition of ℕ with the parent's down-set all follow as one- or three-line specializations. The proof is axiom-free (0 sorries, 0 axiom declarations, no native_decide; #print axioms reports only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound).
conclusion.implications: Stating the inheritance of non-solvability as a covariant property of the carrier — rather than as the isolated fact that S₅ is non-solvable — explains *why* no larger symmetric group can recover solvability: an unsolvable permutation group sits inside every enlargement as a subgroup. Paired with the parent, the result exhibits the entire solvability dichotomy of symmetric and alternating groups as a single order-complement (down-set {≤4} ⊔ up-set {≥5}) meeting at the Abel–Ruffini boundary 5 = 4 + 1. This is the order-theoretic seed from which the classical claim 'the general quintic is not solvable by radicals' inherits its permanence in higher degrees.
openQuestions: Can the same contrapositive packaging be applied to other subgroup-closed properties (nilpotency, supersolvability, having bounded derived length) to produce their own up-set thresholds in the symmetric-group tower?

The threshold 5 is here imported from the grandparent classification; is there a self-contained order-theoretic proof that the least non-solvable cardinality is the successor of the greatest solvable one for an abstract subgroup-closed predicate, independent of the specific value 5?
Does the carrier-functorial framing extend to infinite symmetric groups, where Perm of an infinite set is never solvable — is there a meaningful 'up-set at infinity' completing the finite picture?
